boardStatus: Pain Medicine is a multidisciplinary subspecialty certification jointly recognized by ABA, ABPMR, and ABPN. The ABA administers the shared computer-based examination; each participating board controls its own applicant eligibility and certificate. The public ABA blueprint states 200 single-best-answer questions over four hours, divided 50% General and 50% Clinical States.
boardEligibilityNotice: Completion of this independent course, watching videos, passing its original questions, or completing any planned clip does NOT establish or preserve eligibility, board certification, licensure, clinical privileges, DEA/CDS authority, ACGME credit, fellowship completion, case/procedure volume, or eligibility for any board exam. Johns Hopkins itself says successful completion of its ACGME fellowship does not by itself confer subspecialty certification; applicants must independently meet their primary board’s requirements. Exact published examples: ABPMR requires its diplomate in good standing, a current valid unrestricted U.S./territory/Canada license, 12 months of qualifying ACGME pain fellowship, and program-director recommendation. ABPN requires certification in neurology, child neurology, or psychiatry by December 31 of the preceding year and 12 months ACGME pain training completed by July 31 of the exam year; it currently does not accept international program training. The ABA exam page/blueprint must be consulted for ABA-specific current rules. Requirements, dates, and pathways change; verify directly with the intended board before relying on any plan.

For an ABNS-certified neurosurgeon, the published RFPD post-fellowship pathway additionally requires ABNS certification, an ACGME or CAST CNS-endovascular fellowship, 100 consecutive post-fellowship endovascular cases, recent primary-operator procedure documentation, a written examination, and approved application; other specialties have their own stated pathways. Verify current rules directly with the boards.
